stanzas: পঞ্জাব সিন্ধু গুজরাট মরাঠা দ্রাবিড় উৎকল বঙ্গ
তব শুভ নামে জাগে, তব শুভ আশিষ মাগে,
জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় জয় জয় জয় হে॥
অহরহ তব আহ্বান প্রচারিত, শুনি তব উদার বাণী
হিন্দু বৌদ্ধ শিখ জৈন পারসিক মুসলমান খৃস্টানী
জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় জয় জয় জয় হে॥
পতন-অভ্যুদয়-বন্ধুর পন্থা, যুগ যুগ ধাবিত যাত্রী।
হে চিরসারথি, তব রথচক্রে মুখরিত পথ দিনরাত্রি।
জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় জয় জয় জয় হে॥
ঘোরতিমিরঘন নিবিড় নিশীথে পীড়িত মূর্ছিত দেশে
জাগ্রত ছিল তব অবিচল মঙ্গল নতনয়নে অনিমেষে।
জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় জয় জয় জয় হে॥
গাহে বিহঙ্গম, পূণ্য সমীরণ নবজীবনরস ঢালে।
জয় জয় জয় হে জয় রাজেশ্বর ভারতভাগ্যবিধাতা!
জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় হে, জয় জয় জয় জয় হে॥
orig.credit: Rabindranath Tagore (1911), Gitabitan; the national anthem of India is its first stanza

stanzas: Thou art the ruler of the minds of all people, dispenser of India's destiny. Thy name rouses the hearts of the Panjaub, Sind, Gujarat and Maratha, of the Dravida and Orissa and Bengal; it echoes in the hills of the Vindhyas and Himalayas, mingles in the music of the Jamuna and Ganges and is chanted by the waves of the Indian Sea. They pray for thy blessings and sing thy praise. The saving of all people waits in thy hand, thou dispenser of India's destiny.

Day and night thy voice goes out from land to land calling the Hindus, Buddhists, Shikhs and Jains round thy throne and the Parsees, Mussalmans and Christians. The East and West join hands in their prayer to thee, and the garland of love is woven. Thou bringest the hearts of all people into the harmony of one life, thou dispenser of India's destiny.

The procession of pilgrims passes over the endless road rugged with the rise and fall of nations; and it resounds with the thunder of thy wheels, Eternal Charioteer! Through the dire days of doom thy trumpet sounds and men are led by thee across death. Thy finger points the path to all people, Oh dispenser of Indias destiny!

The darkness was dense and deep was the night. My country lay in a deathlike silence of swoon. But thy mother arms were round her and thine eyes gazed upon her troubled face in sleepless love through her hours of ghastly dreams. Thou art the companion and the saviour of the people in their sorrows, thou dispenser of India's destiny,

The night fades; the light breaks over the peaks of the Eastern hills; the birds begin to sing and the morning breeze carries the breath of new life. The rays of thy mercy have touched the waking land with their blessings. Victory to the King of Kings, Victory to thee, dispenser of India's destiny.
en.credit: Rabindranath Tagore's own translation, The Morning Song of India (1919)

stanzas: pañjāba sindhu gujarāṭa marāṭhā drābiṛa utkala baṅga
taba śubha nāme jāge, taba śubha āśiṣa māge,
jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa he.
aharaha taba āhbāna pracārita, śuni taba udāra bāṇī
hindu bauddha śikha jaina pārasika musalamāna khr̥sṭānī
jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa he.
patana-abhyudaẏa-bandhura panthā, yuga yuga dhābita yātrī.
he cirasārathi, taba rathacakre mukharita patha dinarātri.
jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa he.
ghoratimiraghana nibiṛa niśīthe pīṛita mūrchita deśe
jāgrata chila taba abicala maṅgala natanaẏane animeṣe.
jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa he.
gāhe bihaṅgama, pūṇya samīraṇa nabajībanarasa ḍhāle.
jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa he jaẏa rājeśbara bhāratabhāgyabidhātā!
jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa he, jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa jaẏa he.

notes: en is null: Tagore's own translation (The Morning Song of India, part 'en') is used. It is prose, 2 paragraphs a stanza (2/2/2/2/2 against orig's 7/6/6/6/6), so it cannot be set line against line.

Romanization: ISO 15919 as a transliteration of the Bengali letters, not of the sung pronunciation: the inherent vowel is written wherever the script has no hasanta (jaẏa, taba; sung roughly 'joy', 'tobo'); ব is b throughout (bidhātā, not vidhātā), as Bengali has no separate v letter; য় is ẏ, য is y, ড় ṛ, ঢ় ṛh, ং ṁ, ঁ m̐, ৃ r̥, ৎ t; conjuncts with ব-phalā are written letter by letter (āhbāna, śaṅkhadhbani, duḥsbapne, rājeśbara). Compounds are one word where the source writes them so, its hyphens kept. The dandas । and ॥ are given as full stops.
Readers who know the anthem's usual Hindi-style romanization ('Jana Gana Mana Adhinayaka Jaya He, Bharata Bhagya Vidhata') will find this stricter; the editor may want a line saying so.
line 5.2: the source spells 'পূণ্য' (pūṇya) for the usual 'পুণ্য' (puṇya, 'holy'); romanized as written.
line 2.2: 'খৃস্টানী' (khr̥sṭānī), Christians, is the source's spelling; kept as written.
